source_text:
[tense] This town has always had this old dumpster full of junk. Piles of trash, car wheels, metal doors, and plastic. You can find almost anything in here if you search long enough, but almost no one comes here. That’s precisely why I figured this could be the perfect hiding place for the murderer.

I thought I’d be alone, but apparently I’ve got some company. I spot the town’s hobo leaning against a broken car, probably drunk. I wondered if it wouldn’t be best to just ignore him.

I decided to...

...find the murderer’s hideout.

...search for useful junk.

...go talk to the hobo.

I decided to visit our town’s water processing plant. After all, sunflowers need nothing but two things to live: sunshine and water. Since the sun was probably out of reach, I figured the murderer might try to make his move on my sunflower’s only other vulnerability - water.

I went to the abandoned warehouses on the lonely side of town looking for clues, and

saw the sunrise on metal, rust and broken glass, wild dusty bushes, ragged quiet. Then I...

Then I...

saw the sun directing a haze of floating orange dust soaked light towards me. Then I...

saw the street lights buzzing with electric delight over the abandoned and empty streets. I walked through thick darkness broken by cones of yellow. I walked through the futility of it all. Then I...

... sat on a dusty old sofa.

... looked around for clues.

... fed some cats.

... went to the Roller Street warehouse.

I went home and made sure everything was all right. My flat is small, so, living there all alone, not much tends to happen in it. After watering my sunflower, I decided to...

... write down all the clues I had found so far.

... spy on my neighbour.

... search for cameras or traps.

... build a barricade.

I strolled towards the school, an old brick building surrounded by a tall black iron fence.
One is never too old to learn, right? As I got closer I realized how good it felt knowing I was free to walk away whenever I wanted. Upon arriving, I...

...walked up to the main entrance...

...talked with some adults at the gate...

... saw my neighbour talking with a young schoolgirl!

I decided to take a stroll through the town’s park, thinking that perhaps it would help me clear my thoughts. It was almost silent there, except for the refreshing sound of the wind through the leaves. I liked the park even though it had no sunflowers - I had looked.
As I was walking around, I spotted...

... a gardener, tending to his plants.

... a really old lady sitting on a bench.

... my favourite sitting spot.

... a street sweeper, cleaning the park avenue.

... a group of children chasing each other.

My search for new clues led me to the main avenue of the town. Everyone passes through here at some point, so I figured that, logically, the assassin would do so too. As soon as I came to the avenue, my attention was caught by...

I came back to the Avenue. I could feel there was something left for me to do there. As soon as I got there, I headed to...

...a suspicious alleyway...

...a chocolate store...

...an innocent looking girl...

Fermat pizza shop has been there forever. Some say it is a hole full of cockroaches, which is true. It is also the best pizza you can find in town. And the place to be to gather information and gossip.

I went back to the pizza place. It was hot in there.

... write down all the clues I had found so far, to get a clearer picture of my progress.

- I found a cap on some bushes next to the warehouses. It had a sign resembling a sunflower.

- I overheard the street sweeper talking over the phone about a warehouse on Roller Street.

- I gave a sandwich to the hobo, which he ate.

- I saw a car crashing against the mailbox in the main avenue in the afternoon.

- I saw a little girl playing around the main avenue in the afternoon and evening.

- I saw Fermat looking away as I said ''sunflower''. He is hiding something!

- I infiltrated the school and read the little girl’s notebook. She’s the actual mastermind behind the murder of my sunflower.

- I found out my neighbour is part of the complot. She will abseil down and immolate herself and the sunflower at midnight unless I stop her!

- Crazy as it sounds, I think I’m trapped in a time loop, reliving the same 24 hours over and over.

- I saw my neighbour having an allergy attack because of some flowers. She and the street sweeper are lovers!

- A sniper is going to shoot my sunflower if I don’t stop it!
